mechanism.name: per-lane load widening (load-instruction-count reduction) in MatmulVecBF16
mechanism.form: remap each lane from 4-element k-chunks (one uvec2 load per row per iteration, stride 128) to 8-element k-chunks (one 16-byte load per row per iteration, stride 256), cutting total load instructions ~43 percent for k=896
eliminated_by: not bit-preserving: counterexample_K16.npz - shipped sums to 0x0000, widened mapping to 0x4000 (tie-rich adversarial grid, trial 51); a bit-moving remap cannot land because fork short/long pins may only move to native's digest and BF16 1K holds at full strength

no headroom: the kernel already streams at 57.6 GB/s read (whole-submit, in-window) versus 52.1 GB/s aggregate for the same-instrument copy - it is DRAM-bound above copy throughput, so load-instruction count cannot be the limiter
